skill.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skill.description: Guide completed development work through test verification, local merge, pull request creation, branch preservation, or confirmed cleanup.
skill.summary: Finish a tested development branch with a structured Git integration or cleanup workflow.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 24 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, constrained local shell substitutions, and benign standard-device redirection. The documented Git workflow includes explicit confirmation before destructive branch deletion, with no evidence of prompt injection or malicious intent.

static_findings.snippet: git merge-base HEAD main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD master 2>/dev/null

content.value_statement: Completed branches need a clear, verified path to integration or cleanup. This skill checks tests, presents four choices, and executes the selected Git workflow.
actual_capabilities: Runs the project test suite before offering completion choices.
Identifies a likely base branch using Git merge-base.
Offers local merge, pull request, preservation, and discard workflows.
Pushes a selected branch and prepares a pull request with a test plan.
Requires typed confirmation before force-deleting a branch.
Removes associated worktrees after selected completion workflows.
limitations: Requires an existing Git repository with a completed development branch.
Depends on the project test command being available and correctly configured.
Pull request creation requires GitHub CLI authentication and a configured remote.
Base branch detection may require user confirmation for uncommon repository layouts.

use_cases.title: Complete a Solo Feature
use_cases.description: Verify a feature branch, merge it locally, retest the result, and remove the completed branch.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Team Review
use_cases.description: Push tested work and create a pull request with a concise summary and verification plan.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Release Worktrees
use_cases.description: Review completed branches and remove worktrees only after the selected workflow permits cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Finish My Current Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Finish the current development branch. Run the appropriate tests, then present the available integration and cleanup options.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow after completing a small change

prompt_templates.title: Create a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this branch, push it to the configured remote, and create a pull request with a summary and test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Merge Locally and Retest
prompt_templates.prompt: Determine the base branch, verify the feature branch, merge locally, retest the merged result, and clean up the completed branch.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Complex Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the current branch and worktree relationships. Present all completion options, preserve anything uncertain, and require explicit confirmation before destructive actions.

output_examples.input: Finish my current feature branch after checking the tests.
output_examples.output: Tests passed. Choose whether to merge locally, create a pull request, keep the branch, or discard the work.

output_examples.input: Create a pull request for this completed branch.
output_examples.output: The branch was pushed and the pull request was prepared with a change summary and test plan. The worktree remains available.
The branch, listed commits, and worktree will be permanently removed. Type the required confirmation before deletion proceeds.

best_practices: Run the complete relevant test suite before selecting an integration workflow.
Confirm the detected base branch when the repository uses uncommon branch names.
Review branch, commit, and worktree details before confirming permanent deletion.
anti_patterns: Do not merge or open a pull request while required tests are failing.
Do not remove a worktree that must remain available for review or later work.
Do not force-delete a branch without exact, explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after implementation is complete and the branch is ready for testing, integration, review, preservation, or cleanup.

faq.question: Which completion options are available?
faq.answer: The skill offers local merge, pull request creation, keeping the branch unchanged, or confirmed discard.

faq.question: Does the skill continue when tests fail?
faq.answer: No. It reports the failures and stops before offering merge, pull request, or cleanup actions.

faq.question: Can it create a GitHub pull request?
faq.answer: Yes. GitHub CLI must be installed, authenticated, and connected to the repository remote.

faq.question: How does destructive cleanup work?
faq.answer: The skill lists affected work, requests the exact confirmation word, and deletes only after receiving that confirmation.

faq.question: Does it always remove the worktree?
faq.answer: No. Worktree cleanup depends on the selected workflow, and preservation remains available when further work is needed.
